conceptual assets.information: The first source word supplied to a cryptographic operation and retained for its computation, including as the XPERM source. It enters through rs1_i and can leave as selected or permuted data through res_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because XPERM can select slices of the retained operand into xperm_res and res_o at lines 383, 393 and 357, while integrity is at risk because rs1 is reset and captured from rs1_i at lines 304 and 313, so altering that capture changes the cryptographic computation.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe XPERM results to recover operand bytes or alter the captured rs1 value so that the coprocessor produces an incorrect result.

conceptual assets.information: The second source word supplied to a cryptographic operation and retained for its computation, including as a hash operand or S-box and permutation selector. It enters through rs2_i and is not returned unmixed by an output port.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because rs2 is reset and captured from rs2_i at lines 305 and 314, and the captured value is used in the cryptographic result paths at lines 383, 389 and 420-425.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the captured rs2 value or its selection role, causing the cryptographic operation to use the wrong operand or table entry.

conceptual assets.information: The result computed by the selected XPERM, SHA, SM3, AES or SM4 transformation from the source operands. The processor depends on this value being returned through res_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the computed result is exposed on res_o at lines 357, 359, 362 and 364; integrity is at risk because the result is produced by the cryptographic datapaths at lines 393, 413-416, 420-425, 441 and 475 and stored into res_o; availability is at risk because the result register is cleared and only loaded when done is asserted at lines 353-357.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe res_o, corrupt a result datapath or selection, or prevent done from enabling the result write so that the returned value is disclosed, incorrect or withheld.

conceptual assets.information: The internal progress state and completion indication that determine whether a cryptographic operation is idle, busy or complete and when its result is valid. It has no direct entry port because command fields only decide its transitions, and it leaves through valid_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because state and done are assigned and transitioned at lines 308-309, 325, 328, 333 and 336-337, so corruption can release an invalid result; availability is at risk because those same state and completion assignments control whether valid_o is asserted at line 343 and whether result capture proceeds.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the progress state or done indication to complete prematurely with an invalid result or remain inactive so that the operation never reports completion.

conceptual assets.information: The internally decoded decision that a recognized cryptographic instruction is accepted and starts operand capture and execution. It has no entry or exit port because ctrl_i fields only decide the internally generated cmd_valid pulse.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because cmd_valid is generated from the control record and decoded command at line 296 and controls operand capture at line 312 and state entry at lines 323-325; availability is at risk because forcing this decision low prevents the operation from starting.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the command-valid decode to suppress a required cryptographic operation or accept an unintended operation.

considered, not kept.reason: clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the datapath and state, so the Clocks and resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.

considered, not kept.concept: Build-time algorithm enables and S-box constants
considered, not kept.reason: The generics at lines 28-33 and constant S-box tables at lines 59 and 97 only fix immutable build-time implementation behavior, so no runtime RTL element can modify or withhold them.
